title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered, Artifact-Backed Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (and at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The frozen run used gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 within a hosted generate–validate–repair adapter. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes used in the primary analysis = 141. Observed per-pair acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (95.7447%); Guarded 141/141 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. We reconcile preregistration language vs. the formal estimand, disclose a protocol deviation (unset runtime sampling temperature), document executed vs. unexecuted preregistered analyses (benign-control not executed), and discuss operational interpretation and limitations constrained by synthetic scope and single-model/validator evaluation. All principal numeric claims are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts.

sections.introduction:
Generative LLMs promise to translate operator intent into device CLI and thereby reduce manual NetOps effort. However, LLM outputs can violate sequencing constraints, CLI grammar, or safety invariants; adversarial or malformed inputs can exacerbate these risks. Prior prototype work shows that coupling generation with deterministic verification and constrained repair can improve outcome metrics, but published evaluations frequently rely on token-level or reference-match measures that do not directly reflect deployability or validator acceptance [1–4].

This study asks a focused, operational question amenable to preregistered inference: How effective are template-based input sanitization and deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) at changing the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated? The experiment was preregistered (cand-2026-03) and executed under shared_initial_candidate semantics so that each paired comparison isolates post-generation pipeline effects (sanitization, gating, and permitted repair) applied to a single shared LLM draft per adversarial intent. Our contribution is a preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation that (a) reports exact paired counts and inference, (b) traces discordant cases to sanitizer/repair activity, and (c) clarifies interpretive boundaries between validator acceptance and attacker-centric safety.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network-verification methods (Header Space Analysis, VeriFlow, NetPlumber variants) are commonly used to check forwarding and access-control invariants before deployment; they provide semantics-focused acceptance criteria rather than token-level similarity and thus are natural deployment gates for LLM-assisted NetOps [5–7]. Recent LLM-for-NetOps evaluations (NetConfEval, NetLLMBench and related suites) demonstrate that raw model generation produces both syntactic and higher-level semantic errors (ordering, precondition violations, protected-interface breaches), and that generate–validate–repair architectures improve narrow-task outcomes when verifier feedback is actionable [3,8–11]. Security analyses of LLM-integrated systems document prompt-injection and indirect-prompt attacks that motivate sanitization and gating defenses [12]. Surveys of AIOps and telecommunications recommend more operationally grounded benchmarks that measure deployability and validator acceptance rather than token overlap alone [4]. Our design builds on these findings by using a deterministic validator as the formal acceptance oracle and by preregistering a paired estimand centered on validator acceptance.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration. The study was preregistered prior to observing outcomes (preregistration_sha256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where each adversarial intent yields a binary outcome = 1 if the deterministic validator would accept the final candidate for deployment and 0 otherwise. The confirmatory test is an exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes; bootstrap percentile 95% CIs use 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729.

Design and scope. The preregistered design targeted N = 150 adversarial intents (paired episodes). The synthetic intent bank exercises admin, MTU, and VLAN updates under sequencing constraints; the adversary model applied deterministic mutation heuristics to templates. Scope was explicitly limited to these synthetic templates and the deterministic CLI semantics encoded in our validator; no production data were used.

Model, validator, and pipeline semantics. Declared generator: gpt-5-mini; validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5; orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The registered generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate: each pair used one shared LLM draft. The Baseline condition evaluates that shared draft directly with the validator. The Guarded condition applies template-based input sanitization prior to gating; per policy the guarded branch may permit at most one automated repair LLM call before final validation. This shared_initial_candidate design ensures that any paired difference arises only from downstream sanitization/gating/repair steps, not from differing initial generations.

Missingness and exclusions. The preregistered missingness plan excluded a paired unit only when both paired runs were technical failures (model API failure, verifier timeout, or parser error). Provider-call accounting and failure categories were recorded; excluded counts and all technical failures were archived. Critically, the preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed in this run; consequently, no empirical false-positive-blocking rates are reported and any claims requiring that control are omitted from inference.
sections.results:
Execution summary. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; failed episodes = 18. After applying the preregistered exclusion rule (exclude a pair only when both runs failed), 141 complete pairs entered the primary analysis (complete_pairs = 141; both_missing_pairs = 9).

Condition-level outcomes and paired counts. Baseline accepted = 135/141 (0.9574468085106383). Guarded accepted = 141/141 (1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 135 (both accepted), n10 = 6 (guarded accepted, baseline rejected), n01 = 0 (baseline accepted, guarded rejected), n00 = 0 (both rejected). The observed paired point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. All numbers and test parameters are archived in the analysis artifacts.

Discordant-case diagnostics. The six discordant n10 pairs are traceable to sanitizer and/or the single permitted repair calls: repair-stage activity (repair count = 6) aligns with these discordant pairs. For each discordant pair the shared_initial_candidate was identical between Baseline and Guarded, and the guarded pipeline produced a final candidate that the validator accepted whereas the baseline validator rejected the shared draft. Archived validator traces indicate two diagnostic patterns in those discordant cases: (a) sanitizer-caused normalization or slot-filling that restored required fields and thereby enabled acceptance, and (b) single automated repairs whose outputs satisfied the validator. Because the primary estimand is validator acceptance-for-deployment, conversions enabled by repair or sanitization increase guarded acceptance even when they represent recovered benign drafts rather than elimination of adversarial advantage.

Sensitivity to missingness. Nine paired units were excluded due to both-run technical failure. As a conservative (non-preregistered) sensitivity check treating excluded pairs as failures yields baseline acceptance = 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded acceptance = 141/150 = 0.9400; this does not change the observed direction of effect though it reduces absolute rates. The technical failures and sensitivity counts are archived and reported in the execution and analysis manifests.

Unexecuted preregistered items. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore empirical false-positive-blocking rates and the related secondary inferences are absent from these results and from any operational claim relying on them.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and claim boundary. The preregistration's natural-language hypothesis framed verifier-gating as a defense to reduce attacker success; the formal estimand measured validator acceptance-for-deployment. Our results show a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in validator acceptance under the guarded pipeline (≈4.255 percentage points). Diagnostics show this increase arose because sanitizer and bounded repair converted certain drafts the baseline validator rejected into final candidates the validator accepted. Thus, improved validator acceptance does not, on its own, demonstrate reduced attacker success: it can reflect recovery of reparable benign drafts. Operational claims about attacker mitigation therefore require an independent semantic-safety oracle (e.g., reachability or end-to-end attack-success definition) in addition to validator acceptance.

Operational implications. Within this synthetic setting, sanitizer + bounded automated repair can reduce operator rework by converting invalid drafts into validator-accepted candidates. That benefit depends on (i) validator semantic coverage, and (ii) constrained repair scope and auditing to avoid masking adversarial manipulations. The six discordant cases illustrate the trade-off: repairs that restore intended semantics are beneficial; repairs that alter intent-risk semantics require human oversight or stronger semantic oracles.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced effective sample size and triggered preregistered exclusions. Construct validity: the validator encodes CLI grammar, sequencing, and protected-interface invariants but does not capture all protocol-level or dynamic runtime properties; validator acceptance is therefore a partial proxy for operational safety. External validity: single model (gpt-5-mini), single validator, and synthetic intents limit generalization across vendors, dialects, and production conditions. Conclusion validity: a high baseline (ceiling effect) makes absolute gains small even when statistically detectable; operational significance must be weighed against this ceiling.

Reproducibility notes and protocol deviation. The archived model configuration records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (unset); this unset sampling parameter is a protocol deviation because provider defaults can affect sampling. To preserve paired comparability the run used shared_initial_candidate semantics (single generation per pair) and provider-call accounting confirms stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 150, repair = 6. For deterministic reproduction we recommend explicitly setting temperature = 0 in the model configuration and re-running with identical task and orchestration manifests; full execution and analysis manifests are archived for artifact-grounded reproduction.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial-intent bank found that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). Diagnostics tie the observed discordant conversions to sanitizer and permitted repair activity. Importantly, validator acceptance is a partial proxy for safety; an attacker-centric claim requires an independent semantic-safety oracle. Limits include synthetic scope, single-model/validator evaluation, and an unset runtime sampling temperature. Future work should run the preregistered benign-control, adopt an independent semantic-safety oracle for attacker-centric estimands, diversify models and validators, and fix sampling parameters for deterministic reproduction. All principal numbers and reconciliations reported here are supported by the archived execution and analysis artifacts referenced in the manuscript evidence bundle and the archived execution/analysis manifests cited below.

Declared components: primary generator = gpt-5-mini, deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration: study cand-2026-03 was archived prior to observing outcomes (preregistration_sha256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). Protocol deviation: the archived run recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature (temperature = null) in the archived model configuration; this is disclosed because provider-side defaults may affect sampling determinism. To preserve paired comparability the pipeline used shared_initial_candidate semantics (single shared generation per paired intent) and provider-call accounting in the archived reconciliation confirms the executed call pattern. The execution and analysis manifests containing full archived artifacts and machine-readable provenance are available in the artifact bundle associated with this submission. No human manually edited or corrected the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to deterministic mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
